1	# Growth — extract lessons (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's capture stage, over **both** lesson sources in one run: the window's repo activity
4	(commits, merged PRs, issue discussion) and the conversation logs captured from working sessions. Each
5	durable, reusable lesson is folded into the repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/` — the
6	normalized capture surface) at the repo's own level, without straining to generalize it. The run lands its
7	edits through a single PR **delivered to land** (on the default delivery settings it merges once the repo's
8	checks pass, with no human review — daily capture never piles up as review requests); finding nothing to add
9	on a given run is a perfectly good outcome.
10	
11	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding
12	scope**: it names which halves are live, the substantive commit shas and the PRs/issues touched in the
13	window, and whether the retention prune is due. That is the work; do not widen it.
14	
15	> This is the **unattended daily** capture. It writes only the repo's *own* local packs, so — **unlike** an
16	> owner-requested, in-session retrospective (which delivers a PR for a human to review) — it opens a PR and
17	> **delivers it to land** (the shared procedure under *Output* below; on the default settings GitHub lands it
18	> once the repo's checks pass). The shared canon stays human-gated — lifting anything up into it is the
19	> central promote task's job (canon-side), and that PR waits for the owner.
20	
21	## Conventions used in this doc
22	
23	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
24	- **Access split — local git for repo content, MCP for the issue/PR API.** The repo's own content is plain
25	  **local git** in the checkout: the commits, the `conversation-logs` branch and its files
26	  (`git fetch`/`show`/`rm`/`push`), and staging the lesson edits onto a branch. Reading issue/PR activity,
27	  opening the PR and delivering it, posting the exchange summaries and the tracking-issue log go
28	  through the session's **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub
29	  access — the shell reaches only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so
30	  never reach for `gh`/`curl` or a cross-repo clone.
31	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in
32	  [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) — everything
33	  under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
34	  window), the repo's own packs; never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
35	
36	## The run — two source skills, then the upgrade pass
37	
38	The **method** for each source lives in its skill; this worker only frames the run around them. Don't
39	re-derive any of it here.
40	
41	1. **Activity half — the [extract-from-activity](../../skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) skill**, over
42	   exactly the commits, merged PRs and issues named in Context. **Skip this half entirely when Context says
43	   the activity half is not in scope** (a quiet repo whose only reason to run was the retention prune).
44	2. **Conversation half — the [extract-from-conversations](../../skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
45	   skill**, over the repo's captured logs. `git fetch origin conversation-logs`, then list its files
46	   (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/conversation-logs`); no branch, or no `*.jsonl`, and this half is done.
47	   Give each log captured in the recent window a **fresh pass** (its filename carries the capture stamp;
48	   corpus dedup makes an overlapping re-read harmless, so err toward re-reading the last several days), and
49	   post the skill's provenance summary for each rule that actually lands.
50	3. **Retention prune**, when Context says it is due. Read `retention_days` from this repo's
51	   `.claudinite-checks.json` (the grow_with_claudinite entry's `config.retention_days`) — unset means this
52	   step is skipped entirely (capture-only adoption). For each log whose filename stamp is older than
53	   `retention_days` days: give it the **final hindsight pass** the skill describes (anything it still yields
54	   lands like any other keeper), then `git rm` it on the `conversation-logs` branch and push (commit message
55	   ending `[skip ci]`). The branch is never merged and its history is never rewritten — plain add/remove
56	   commits only. This push to the non-default logs branch is outside the outcome taxonomy (DESIGN §1).
57	4. **Upgrade pass — the [prose-to-checks](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) skill, over what *this run*
58	   just wrote.** Both halves route down the local promotion ladder as they go, but a lesson written as prose
59	   under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides. So before opening the PR, take the prose
60	   this run added and ask the skill's questions of it: does it clear the working-rule gate, and does it
61	   constrain a static signature a check could observe? If yes, convert it now — author the rule module,
62	   register it in its pack's `pack.mjs`, prove it with a **see-it-fail** fixture, and apply the deletion
63	   test to the prose the check now stands beside. **Scope is this run's own additions only** — the standing
64	   prose backlog is the weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)'s job, and widening
65	   into it here would duplicate that task's work under an auto-merging PR.
66	
67	If an edit touches something a test reads (a doc constant, a code path), run the repo's offline test suite
68	and keep it green before opening the PR.
69	
70	## Output: one PR, delivered to land
71	
72	If the run found at least one genuinely new lesson, it lands **all** of it — both halves, plus any check the
73	upgrade pass produced — through a **single PR**: one commit for the whole run on a per-run-unique branch, not
74	one per lesson and not one per half. Open the PR (title `Claudinite growth: extract lessons`, its commit
75	referencing the tracking issue so the `task-lifecycle` gate passes), then **deliver it by the shared
76	procedure — [deliver-pr.md](../../../../engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md)**. That procedure — never this file —
77	owns every landing nuance: it reads this repo's `maintenance.delivery` (a `review` repo's PR waits for the
78	owner — still a delivered outcome), arms auto-merge where the repo allows it, and licenses the hand merge
79	when the arm is rejected `clean status` (a base branch that requires nothing — GitHub never auto-merges
80	there). Do not assume this run's PR merges unreviewed: that is the repo's setting, not this task's. On the
81	default settings it squash-merges once the repo's checks pass, so daily lesson-capture never floods review
82	requests while every change still gets a PR trail and a CI gate. This writes only the repo's *own* local
83	packs (not the shared canon). A run that finds nothing and opens nothing is fine — and common.
84	
85	A new check must ship green — see it fail on a violating fixture, pass on a clean one — so CI stays green and
86	the PR can merge; a check that can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.
87	
88	## Tracking: log each run under the task's own issue
89	
90	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
91	
92	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract**
93	
94	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle, and it
95	differs per repo). A run that finds no issue under the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open,
96	close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no meaning, only the log does. When a run adds a lesson,
97	converts one to a check, or prunes logs, log it as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue — so the issue
98	accumulates a scrollable history, each entry naming **what happened and where**. A run that changed nothing
99	logs nothing. (A repo that still carries a closed `Claudinite tracker: Conversation Extract` issue from when
100	the halves were two tasks keeps it as history — never post to it, never reopen it.)
101	
102	## Run on a capable model
103	
104	Deciding whether a lesson is genuinely new and durable — and deduping it against what's already documented —
105	is a **judgment call**, not mechanical extraction. A downgraded model adds noise or restates what's there,
106	and **on the default delivery no human reviews the PR before it lands** — CI gates correctness, not whether a
107	"lesson" earns its keep — so the capable-model requirement matters all the more. This task declares
108	`agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
109	
110	## What this task must never do
111	
112	- **Never touch the shared canon** — this task writes only the repo's *own* local packs under
113	  `.claudinite/local/packs/`; everything else under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mount, and lifting a
114	  lesson up into the canon is the central promote task's job.
115	- **Never widen past the Context window** — the halves it declares live, the substantive commits and the
116	  touched PRs/issues named there are the scope; do not re-decide it. That includes the upgrade pass: this
117	  run's own additions, never the standing backlog.
118	- **Never merge `conversation-logs`** anywhere, and never rewrite its history — plain add and remove commits only.
119	- **Never paste the conversation onto an issue** — not raw JSONL, not a rendered transcript, not the turns
120	  themselves. Each landed rule gets one ≤200-word summary of the exchange behind it, and nothing more.
121	- **Never delete a log younger than retention, and never delete anything while `retention_days` is unset** —
122	  deletion is the ack that both passes happened.
123	- **Don't add noise** — a duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, the more so when
124	  its PR usually lands with no human review to catch it.
125

1	---
2	name: extract-from-activity
3	description: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
4	---
5	
6	# Extract lessons from repo activity
7	
8	The **artifact** half of lesson extraction: mine what a window of work left behind — commits, the PRs
9	merged in it, the issue discussion around them — for durable, reusable lessons, and fold each into the
10	repo's **own local packs**. Its sibling [extract-from-conversations](../extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
11	mines the *dialogue*; this one never sees a conversation, only what the work committed.
12	
13	The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
14	surface lives are shared with that sibling and stay canonical in
15	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't re-derive it. What follows is only
16	what reading *artifacts* adds.
17	
18	## Capture at the repo's own level
19	
20	Write each lesson at whatever level reads naturally for this repo — refer to its files, services, or
21	mechanics wherever that's what makes the lesson clear. Don't force either extreme: don't contort a lesson
22	to be hyper-specific, and don't polish it into a general, portable rule. Making a lesson portable is the
23	growth lifecycle's **promote** stage, done canon-side later over whatever merged here; here, just capture
24	it usefully and let promotion lift whatever turns out to travel.
25	
26	## Read the window — and read merged PRs properly
27	
28	Work only the window you were handed (a scheduled run gets it as binding scope in the dispatch issue's
29	Context; an owner's ask names it in words). Never widen it.
30	
31	1. **The commits** — full bodies, and the diff wherever a fix is non-obvious.
32	2. **The PRs merged in the window** — read these *first* and read them *whole*: the diff **and** the
33	   review discussion. A merged PR is usually the window's richest lesson source, because it records what
34	   was tried, what a reviewer pushed back on, and why the landed shape won. A verdict reached in review
35	   is a lesson already argued; the commit alone shows only the winner.
36	3. **The issue activity** it names — the comments changed on those numbers.
37	
38	## What artifacts signal — and what they don't
39	
40	The signals worth converting here are the ones an artifact can carry: a fix whose diff is small but whose
41	*reason* is not obvious from the code; a review comment that names a convention the author missed; a
42	revert or a follow-up fix that says the first shape was wrong; a PR that grew several rounds because its
43	approach was re-decided mid-flight.
44	
45	**An already-settled, already-enforced implementation choice is not a lesson.** If a check or a test
46	already pins the shape — which roots a CI sweep walks, which contract a construction must satisfy — and
47	all that is left to say is *why it looks like that*, that explanation belongs as a comment at the
48	implementation site, not as prose in a pack. A rule earns its place by steering a **future** decision or
49	catching a **repeatable** mistake, not by narrating a past one that is already locked in.
50	
51	Wall-time and dialogue friction (a clarifying round-trip, a backtrack, a wait sat through) leave no trace
52	in a diff. Don't infer them from artifacts — that is the conversation sibling's territory, working from
53	logs that actually carry the timestamps.
54	
55	## Landing it
56	
57	Route each keeper down the ladder in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — check first,
58	then pack skill, prose last — into the local pack whose territory owns it. Write more checks and less
59	prose, and keep each addition terse and in the repo's own voice.
60	
61	A new check ships **green or not at all**: see it fail on a violating fixture and pass on a clean one. A
62	rule that cannot be made confident lands as prose instead — never as a broken check.
63	
64	Finding nothing is a perfectly good and common outcome; a duplicate or invented "lesson" is worse than
65	adding nothing.
66

1	---
2	name: extract-from-conversations
3	description: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
4	---
5	
6	# Extract lessons from a conversation
7	
8	The **dialogue** half of lesson extraction: read one agent ↔ user session — its turns *and* the actions
9	taken in it — and convert its friction into changes that make the **next** run faster, clearer, and less
10	dependent on human steering. Its sibling [extract-from-activity](../extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) mines
11	what the work committed; this one mines how the work went.
12	
13	The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
14	surface lives stay canonical in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't
15	re-derive it. What follows is only what reading a *conversation* adds.
16	
17	## The goal
18	
19	Every pass optimizes for one outcome: **the next run needs less.** Less clarification, less rework, less
20	waiting, less human steering. Read the session not as "what did we accomplish" but as "where did this
21	cost more than it should have, and what durable change removes that cost next time." If a pass can't name
22	a concrete next-time saving, it found nothing — and that's fine.
23	
24	## Where the conversation comes from
25	
26	- **A captured log** on the repo's orphan `conversation-logs` branch (`<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`),
27	  read with plain git in the checkout — `git show origin/conversation-logs:<file>`. The log carries
28	  per-entry timestamps, per-message token usage, and the `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs behind every
29	  wall-time number, which is exactly what the measured analysis below needs. This is the routine path.
30	- **The live session**, when an owner asks in plain words for a retrospective. Same method; deliver the
31	  capture as a branch + PR **for a human to review**, never one that self-merges.
32	
33	**Never reflect-and-edit unprompted in the middle of a task** — it interrupts the work; the owner decides
34	when a session is done enough to mine.
35	
36	## What to look for — the friction signals
37	
38	Read the conversation end to end and hunt for these signatures. Each marks a place the loop cost more than
39	necessary, and each converts to a specific durable fix.
40	
41	### 1. Misunderstandings between agent and user
42	
43	The signs: a clarifying-question round-trip; the user correcting an assumption ("no, I meant…"); the agent
44	building the wrong thing and reworking it; the user restating the same request; an `AskUserQuestion` whose
45	answer was, in hindsight, the obvious default.
46	
47	**Convert to:** encode the resolved understanding so the next agent never has to ask. Every question the
48	user answered is a candidate **default**; every correction is a candidate **convention or glossary entry**;
49	a recurring wrong assumption is a candidate **confirm-first checkpoint placed earlier**, or a clearer doc
50	the agent reads cold and gets right the first time. The test of a good fix: next time the agent proceeds
51	correctly **without the round-trip**.
52	
53	### 2. Suboptimal agent actions
54	
55	The signs: the agent took an approach then backtracked; did redundant or repeated work; re-ran a command
56	that had already failed for a knowable reason; reached for a heavy tool where a light one fit; reinvented
57	something the codebase already provided; re-read a file it had just written to "verify"; missed an existing
58	convention and had it corrected in review.
59	
60	**Convert to:** a rule pointing at the right approach or tool, a pointer to the existing helper/convention
61	so it's found first, or a **footgun note placed where it'll be read** (the usage-site-vs-central call is in
62	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). The test: next time the agent takes the good path
63	first, not after a detour.
64	
65	### 3. Long wall-time waits — and measure them
66	
67	The signs: independent operations run **serially** that had no dependency and could have been parallel; a
68	padded fixed `sleep` that over- or under-shot; a process **waited out after its result was already in
69	hand**; blind long polling; re-running a check (e.g. CI) that was already green.
70	
71	**Measure, don't hand-wave.** Quantify the wait with real wall-clock numbers from the log's own timestamps
72	and separate the kinds of time — compute (a compile, a test/render run) vs. genuine **idle waiting**
73	(sleeps, polling, a finished process not yet killed). The numbers are computable, never estimated. A fix is
74	only credible against numbers; name the **single highest-leverage change** that shortens it, or conclude it
75	was already optimal.
76	
77	**Convert to:** a batch/parallelize rule, a poll-with-rolling-backoff instead of a blind sleep,
78	kill-the-process-once-its-output-is-in-hand, or merge-on-an-already-green-check. (These are the subject of
79	the standing **efficiency analysis** in [the unattended-agents skill](../unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — fold
80	a wall-time finding into that frame rather than re-deriving it.) The test: same result, less wall clock, no
81	loss of quality.
82	
83	## Encode the questions the user keeps asking
84	
85	The single highest-leverage move for **less human feedback**: the questions a user asks *repeatedly* are a
86	checklist the agent should run **itself.** If the user keeps asking "how many processes ran — could it be
87	fewer?", "what took longest?", "did you kill it the moment its work was done?", stop waiting to be asked —
88	fold those exact questions into a **standing self-check the agent answers proactively** at the end of the
89	relevant work, and close with a terse verdict (a concrete change, or an explicit "already optimal"). Each
90	recurring question converted this way is one the user never has to ask again — and it's where a *measured*
91	retrospective comes from: the user's recurring efficiency questions, answered pre-emptively, with numbers.
92	
93	## Two passes per log, and the second one may overturn the first
94	
95	A captured log gets a **fresh pass** within a day of capture and a **final hindsight pass** just before
96	retention deletes it, against the corpus as it stands by then. The hindsight pass is a real re-read, not a
97	formality: a friction signal that looked situational the first time may have recurred since, and a lesson
98	landed since may have made a keeper redundant. Both directions are legitimate outcomes.
99	
100	## Provenance: summarize the exchange, never paste it
101	
102	For each rule that actually **lands** from a log, post one short comment on the issue the log names
103	(`--issue-<n>--` in its filename; **`--issue-0--` means the capture had no associated issue**, so there is
104	nothing to post on and the rule simply lands without a comment):
105	
106	- one provenance line — the rule added, the capture date, the session id;
107	- then a **200-word-max** description of just the slice of conversation that caused the rule: what was
108	  asked, what went wrong or got corrected, and why the rule follows from it.
109	
110	**Summarize, never transcribe.** The dialogue itself is far too verbose for an issue — no pasted turns
111	beyond a short quoted phrase, never raw JSONL, never a rendered transcript. A log that yields nothing gets
112	**no** comment: extraction is the only path to permanence, and a log's conversation is gone once retention
113	deletes it. That is a deliberate call, so a padded "lesson" written to feel productive costs more than the
114	silence it replaced.
115

1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
29	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
30	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
31	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
32	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
33	
34	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
35	
36	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
37	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
38	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
39	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
40	
41	1. **A check** in that pack's rules — author the `.mjs`, list it on the pack's `pack.mjs`, ship it with a
42	   red-first fixture. Its failure message *is* the lesson.
43	2. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
44	3. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — only what neither of the above can carry.
45	
46	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
47	relocates it. When no pack's scope fits and the lesson warrants segregation, a new local pack is a
48	self-contained directory drop.
49	
50	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all.** A trap from misusing a specific API, class, or
51	library goes as a **comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where the next editor of
52	that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list. Co-locate it in a file's own header
53	comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a
54	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
55	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
56	
57	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
58	
59	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
60	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
61	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
62	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.
63

1	# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request
2	
3	How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
4	delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
5	run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
6	the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
7	your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
8	lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.
9	
10	## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest
11	
12	Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:
13	
14	- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
15	  applies to you.
16	- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
17	  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
18	  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
19	
20	## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference
21	
22	`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:
23	
24	- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
25	- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
26	  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
27	  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
28	- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
29	  materializing it is baselining's converge job, not yours.
30	- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
31	  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
32	  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the dispatch issue.
33	
34	## 2. Arm auto-merge
35	
36	Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
37	it once this repo's required checks pass.
38	
39	## 3. When the arm is rejected
40	
41	- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
42	  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
43	  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
44	  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
45	  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
46	- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
47	  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
48	  PR's **head sha**:
49	  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
50	    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
51	  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
52	    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
53	  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
54	    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
55	    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
56	    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
57	    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
58	    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
59	    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the `merged-pr` ceiling — the trail
60	    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
61	    unseen check does not survive anything.
62	
63	## Never
64	
65	Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
66	arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
67	manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
68	are always legal outcomes.
69

{"number":157,"title":"growth-dedup: prune local items now covered by canon","body":"Weekly growth-dedup run. Context named these four canon packs as the yardstick for this run (dispatch issue #149): `claude-code-web-users-support`, `basics`, `grow_with_claudinite`, `github-actions`. Every local pack under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (`laughcounter`, `macos-audio`, `on-device-privacy`) was checked against them. Two items were **stripped**; nothing else overlapped these four packs closely enough to prune with confidence — when unsure, the item was left alone.

## Stripped

### `.claudinite/local/packs/laughcounter/RULES.md` — the "nothing runs on `pull_request`" lesson

The lesson's middle clause read:

> That is the repo's shape, not a fault, **and the canon's delivery procedure already licenses the squash merge yourself in exactly that case — take it rather than escalating**: PR #138 sat unmerged for a day...

`grow_with_claudinite`'s `unattended-agents` skill now states this generally:

> "Where a shared delivery procedure exists (Claudinite's `engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md`), the merges it licenses — **like the direct merge on a base branch that requires nothing, where the arm is rejected 'clean status' by design** — are the sanctioned path, not a workaround; anything outside them stays unlanded."
> — `.claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`

That's exactly LaughCounter's rejected-arm scenario, generalized. Stripped the now-canon-owned clause; kept the residue — this repo's own workflow shape (no `pull_request` trigger anywhere), the PR #138 incident (a run misread its own task file's blanket "never hand-merge" as covering this too), and the corollaries about maintenance-PR timing and "CI won't catch it outside `mac/**`" — none of which the canon states.

### `.claudinite/local/packs/on-device-privacy/RULES.md` — "The disclosure must stay true"

The paragraph read:

> **The disclosure must stay true.** `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` and `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` tell the user audio is analysed on-device and not recorded.

`basics/RULES.md` now states the general rule this leans on this repo's two usage-string names to make:

> "A user-facing statement about what the software does with a user's data — a permission prompt's usage string, a privacy policy, a store-listing disclosure — is part of the behaviour's contract, not documentation of it. Change the behaviour and the statement changes in the same commit; a stale disclosure is worse than a blunt one. And read the direction the other way too: retaining something previously not retained, adding an outbound connection, or opening a listener is a change to the promise, not a new field — it earns an explicit decision, and the disclosure rewrite, before the code."
> — `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/RULES.md`

{"number":158,"title":"Claudinite growth: discover local pack laugh-detection","body":"Refs #150. Tracked on the standing log, #44.

## The gap

Manifested this repo's stack from its own files, then held it against the canon shelf (`basics`, `barriers`, `claude-code-web-users-support`, `git-github`, `github-actions`, `grow_with_claudinite`, `tidy-repo`) and the three existing local packs. One domain came out genuinely core and genuinely unowned: **the decision layer between Apple's built-in sound classifier and a number on the menu bar**.

- `local/macos-audio` owns getting audio out of the device safely.
- `local/on-device-privacy` owns the boundary that audio never crosses.
- `local/laughcounter` owns the repo's build, packaging and check-authoring lessons.
- Nothing owned what turns a stream of per-window confidences into discrete, counted, attributed laughs — which is exactly where every count is right or wrong, because the model is a black box that cannot be retrained (`docs/DESIGN-AND-TRADEOFFS.md` §2). The thresholds, the hysteresis, the class-identifier matching, the episode timing and the you-vs-TV attribution *are* the product.

## What landed

`.claudinite/local/packs/laugh-detection/`, declared as `local/laugh-detection` in `.claudinite-checks.json`. Distilled from `mac/Sources/LaughCounter/` (`LaughCounter.swift`, `LaughDetector.swift`, `Store.swift`), `docs/DESIGN-AND-TRADEOFFS.md` §2/§3, the README's *How it works*, and issues #5 (log overhaul, real durations) and #7 (TV de-confliction).

**Checks (3)** — each red-first fixtured and quiet on the repo's real sources:

| Check | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `counting-core-clock-free` | `LaughCounter.swift` imports only `Foundation` and never reads the wall clock — its time comes from `SNClassificationResult.timeRange` via the observation. That is what makes a duration the length of the *laugh* rather than of the analysis backlog, and what keeps the counting rules exercisable without a live microphone. |
| `classifier-keywords-lowercase` | The taxonomy match runs against `identifier.lowercased()`, so a keyword carrying a capital can never fire — a laugh class or a TV-context class silently stops being recognised, with no error. Covers any future keyword list by name. |
| `hysteresis-contract` | `exitThreshold < enterThreshold <= countThreshold` (invert the first pair and one laugh shatters into several; invert the second and the candidate band disappears), and `mergeGap` must exceed the classifier's ~1.5s window hop or every overlapping window becomes its own duplicate laugh. |

**Prose (`RULES.md`, 6)** — improve the decision, not the call into the model (a miss is *near the bar* or *at the model's floor*, and the fix differs) · match sound classes as lowercased stems, never whole words · the counter is handed time, it never asks what time it is · an episode is a laugh, a window is not · never drop a sub-threshold episode, log it as a `candidate` · attribution labels an event, it never suppresses one · the laugh log is a fixed-order, hand-rendered JSONL record.

**No skill** — nothing here has a nameable procedural trigger of its own.

## Verification

- `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/laugh-detection/pack.test.mjs` → 11 pass, 0 fail. Every check fires on a violating fixture and stays silent on the real `mac/Sources/` tree.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` → clean, exit 0, with the pack declared.

**Auto-merge deliberately not armed** — this ships three new checks that reach every Stop hook and every CI run in this repo the moment it merges, so the reviewer is the point.

{"number":159,"title":"Prose-to-checks: convert 2 rules to checks","body":"Weekly prose-to-checks sweep over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the three local packs: `laughcounter`, `macos-audio`, `on-device-privacy`). Two always-testable halves of `macos-audio` prose became checks; nothing else changed.

## What was converted

**`macos-audio/input-node-confined`** (blocking) — only `mac/Sources/LaughCounter/AudioHub.swift` may reach `engine.inputNode`, from *"Never open the device to ask a question about it."* Reading `inputNode` materializes the input node, which opens the default input and mints a hidden coreaudiod aggregate device — the one mechanism by which this app could plausibly wedge a mic.

This is **not** already covered by its sibling `engine-construction-confined`, and per this repo's own lesson ("already covered by another check is a claim to test, not to reason out") the claim was tested by handing that check a violating file:

```swift
func probeRate(engine: AVAudioEngine) -> Double {
    engine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0).sampleRate
}
```

opens the device without ever constructing an engine, and `engine-construction-confined` stays silent on it. A fixture pins that gap so the two checks can't be collapsed by the same reasoning again.

**`macos-audio/swift-toolchain-gate`** (blocking) — a `command -v swift` / `which swift` probe in a shell script or workflow must sit behind an `xcode-select -p` gate, from *"Assume no toolchain on the machine that runs it."* `/usr/bin/swift` ships on every Mac as a stub: it reports success without a developer directory and pops an 8 GB command-line-tools install — at the person diagnosing a dead microphone.

## See-it-fail

Red-first fixtures in `.claudinite/local/packs/macos-audio/pack.test.mjs` (19 tests, all green): each check fires on a violating input, stays quiet on a clean one, and stays quiet on the **real** tree. The real-tree fixture earned its keep immediately — the first draft of `swift-toolchain-gate` flagged the `#` comment in `mac/scripts/diagnose-mic.sh` that *documents* the trap, which is why the check now strips comments before matching (in both directions: a commented-out gate is not a gate).

Verified offline: `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/macos-audio/pack.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/on-device-privacy/pack.test.mjs` → 33/33 pass; `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` → clean, exit 0, with both new rules listed in `--list`.

## Deletion test: no prose deleted

Applied to both paragraphs the new checks now stand beside; both **stay whole**, because each carries something the check cannot encode:

- *"Never open the device to ask a question about it"* also routes availability questions to `AudioDiagnostics`' HAL property queries, carries the ~210-opens-over-3h40m measurement, and states the general value the check can't judge — the cost of an answer is a property of the API you ask, not of how often you ask.
- *"Assume no toolchain on the machine that runs it"* also carries the design rule that anything needed to diagnose a live failure is either shell built into macOS or compiled into the app by CI (why the HAL reads live in `AudioDiagnostics`, not a helper script).

Trimming either to just the sentence the check replaced is exactly what the deletion test forbids. The only prose edit is the pack intro sentence, which enumerated "the three mechanical parts" and would now be wrong.

## Considered and left as prose

- **laughcounter** — all eight lessons are working discipline with no static signature (in-flight process: read `git diff --cached --stat` after `git add -A`; judgment: re-ask a "not statically checkable" verdict after the tree changes; check-authoring style: prefer a positive whitelist). The `pull_request`-triggers lesson would only pin today's workflow shape.
- **macos-audio "Deferred work must be generation-guarded"** — the strongest near-miss. All four `asyncAfter` closures in `AppDelegate` do capture `restartGeneration`, but `Chime` and `VoiceCommand` legitimately defer work that has nothing to guard, so the check would have to scope by filename — pinning today's layout, and unable to decide which deferred work touches the mic. Left as prose.
- **on-device-privacy** — the remaining prose is the product's own privacy requirement (`NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` must stay true, what may cross the boundary), which the sweep's first gate routes to the spec, not to a check.

References #152.

1	# Working in this repo
2	
3	The general lessons this repo has paid for once. The privacy boundary — the
4	product's defining constraint — has its own pack (`local/on-device-privacy`);
5	what follows is everything else.
6	
7	**Don't prune a `.gitignore` section in the same breath as deleting what it
8	ignored — the artifacts are still on disk.** Removing a toolchain (the Python
9	reference, a build system, a generator) invites tidying its ignore rules away in
10	the same commit, but the ignored artifacts it already produced are usually still
11	sitting untracked in the worktree — earlier test runs leave `__pycache__/`,
12	builds leave `build/`. The moment those rules go, the next `git add -A` sweeps
13	the artifacts *into* the very commit that was supposed to remove them, and
14	nothing complains: the commit is valid, the tests still pass, and the junk only
15	shows up as an inflated file count in the diff a reviewer reads. Delete the
16	artifacts from the worktree first (or `git clean` them), then drop their ignore
17	lines — and read `git diff --cached --stat` after any bulk `git add -A`, not just
18	`git status`, since staged additions are exactly what a clean `git status` stops
19	telling you about.
20	
21	**"Not statically checkable" is a verdict about the tree's shape at the time, not
22	about the rule — re-ask it after the tree changes.** `on-device-privacy`'s
23	"everything lives in one deletable directory" sat as prose because proving it
24	looked like it needed data-flow tracking of a `FileManager` write target back to
25	its declaration — true while the Python reference had many entry points, and
26	false the moment that tree went away: the native app has exactly two persistent
27	path roots, both the same search-path lookup, so constraining the *root*
28	constrains every path derived from it and no tracing is needed. A removal, a
29	migration, or a consolidation can collapse the entry points a rule has to cover,
30	so when a sweep meets prose a previous sweep left behind, re-derive the objection
31	against today's sources instead of trusting the recorded verdict.
32	
33	**"Already covered by another check" is a claim to test, not to reason out — hand
34	the sibling check a violating file before dropping a rule as a duplicate.** Three
35	sweeps in a row left `on-device-privacy`'s "the app listens on no socket" as
36	prose, each reasoning that an `NWListener` needs `import Network` and
37	`no-network-client` already bans that. True of that one API, false of the
38	capability: `socket(2)` comes free with `import Foundation` (Darwin is
39	re-exported), `NSXPCListener`/`CFSocket*`/`NSSocketPort` are Foundation types, and
40	an embedded HTTP server arrives as its own import — a file whose entire content
41	was `let fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0)` passed `check_the_world`
42	untouched. A ban list only covers the routes whoever wrote it thought of, so the
43	routes it misses are invisible to exactly the reasoning that drew it; running it
44	against a file that breaks the rule costs a minute and is the only step that can
45	disagree with you.
46	
47	**Write a check as a positive whitelist over an enumerated API surface, not as a
48	list of the bad cases.** `single-storage-directory` flags any search-path lookup
49	whose directory argument is not the literal `.applicationSupportDirectory`,
50	rather than enumerating the directories we don't want. Matching the allowed case
51	buys two things a ban list can't: a `SearchPathDirectory` case that doesn't exist
52	yet is caught the day it lands, and a non-literal argument (`urls(for: dir, in:)`)
53	becomes a finding too — indirection is precisely what would otherwise defeat the
54	check, so refusing to reason about it is a feature. Only invert this where the
55	allowed set is genuinely open-ended.
56	
57	**Ship a version the running app can state, and bump it whenever a build has to be
58	told apart from the last one.** Diagnosing the `installTap` crash (#61) stalled on
59	"which binary is installed?", and the answer had to be reconstructed by grepping a
60	crash report's symbol names for whether `finishListening` took a `generation:`
61	argument. Two causes, both durable. The menu header said only "LaughCounter"; and
62	several genuinely different builds all reported `0.2.1`, because the release
63	workflow keys its Release on `v<version>` read from `mac/Resources/Info.plist` — so
64	a merge that leaves `CFBundleShortVersionString` alone **refreshes the same
65	Release**, and the DMG behind the `latest/download` link changes identity without
66	changing its name. So the menu renders `LaughCounter v<version> (<build>)` from
67	`Bundle.main` rather than a constant in the source — `Info.plist` is already where
68	the version lives and where the release tag comes from, and a second copy could
69	disagree with the DMG it shipped in — and the **build number** is what separates
70	two builds that share a version string, so show it and raise it too. (#74/#75)
71	
72	**A scheduled job that *skips* its work still exits 0 — read what a green run says
73	it did.** This repo's Claudinite scheduler ran green every night while silently
74	skipping baselining, logging "no vendored mount (no stamp)" about a repo whose
75	`.claudinite-checks.json` carried one: the vendored `loadConfig` validated
76	`claudinite` as a legal settings key and then dropped it from the object it
77	returned, so the stamp read `undefined` and the run took the branch meant for a
78	pre-adoption repo. Nothing was red and nothing was missing — the only evidence was
79	one skip line in a log nobody opens on a green run. Two things follow. A *skip* is
80	a finding to read, not a pass: a job whose success and whose no-op look identical
81	from outside is telling you nothing. And when the bug lives inside the mechanism
82	that updates itself, the ordinary route is unreachable — baselining is what
83	refreshes the vendored mount, and the bug was *in* the mount — so the fix has to be
84	pushed in out of band rather than waited for. (#56)
85	
86	**Nothing in this repo runs on `pull_request`, so most PRs carry no checks at all
87	— and arming auto-merge on one is rejected every time.** `build-macos-dmg.yml`
88	and `release-macos-dmg.yml` trigger on `push` scoped to `mac/**` (plus their own
89	file), and `claudinite-scheduler.yml` only on `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch`; no
90	workflow here declares a `pull_request` trigger. A PR touching only
91	`.claudinite/`, `docs/` or `dev/` therefore starts nothing, is mergeable the
92	second it opens, and GitHub answers the auto-merge arm with *"already in clean
93	status — auto-merge only applies when checks are pending."* That is the repo's
94	shape, not a fault. PR #138 sat unmerged for a day because a run read its task
95	file's blanket "never hand-merge" as covering the rejection too. Two
96	corollaries. The maintenance PRs the Action opens land **within seconds** of
97	being armed, so by the time the agent stage starts there is usually no open
98	`claudinite/maintenance-*` PR left to
99	continue on and the condition that escalated no longer reproduces — three cycles
100	running (#127/#128, #129/#130, #133/#134) spent their budget hunting the PR API
101	for a branch that had already merged, when the first move is to fetch `main` and
102	re-run the check against it. And "CI will catch it" is simply false outside
103	`mac/**`: nothing runs, so whatever a change needed proving, prove it locally
104	before it lands. (#137/#138)
105	
106	**That licensed hand-merge comes back as a `[Merge Without Review]` security
107	warning — expect it, and hand the reader the three facts that settle it.** When a
108	scheduled task squash-merges its own PR after the arm is rejected `clean status`,
109	the harness prefixes the subagent's completion notification to the executor with
110	*"SECURITY WARNING … [Merge Without Review] … relying only on its own project-doc
111	citation rather than actual user authorization."* Because nothing here triggers on
112	`pull_request`, every arm is rejected and every `merged-pr` task ends this way, so
113	the warning is **structural** — it arrives on every run that lands anything, and it
114	is silent about whether this particular merge was licensed. Treating it as either a
115	verdict or a rubber stamp is the mistake. Settle it in one read: the delivering
116	agent states the three licensing facts up front in its final report — this repo's
117	`maintenance.delivery` value, the arm rejection verbatim, and the dispatch's
118	declared outcome ceiling — and whoever reads the warning checks those three instead
119	of re-deriving the license from scratch (the 2026-08-08 run's executor spent five
120	extra tool calls re-reading `deliver-pr.md`, the PR and `verify-outcome.mjs` to get
121	back to the same answer). What it must never do is make a run *reverse* a merge
122	decision it already reasoned through — that failure has its own cost here, and its
123	name is #138. (#143/#144)
124	
125	**Nothing you post to GitHub can be edited afterwards — resolve every value before
126	the comment goes up.** The MCP GitHub toolset these runs use has
127	`add_issue_comment` and **no comment-update tool at all**, so a comment that goes
128	out wrong can only be appended to. A run claiming issue #143 wrote the placeholder
129	`2026-08-08T00:00:00Z` into its claim comment meaning to correct it after, found no
130	edit tool, and left the issue permanently carrying both the wrong timestamp and a
131	"Correction:" comment under it. An agent session has no ambient clock — `date -u
132	+"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"` is one Bash call and the only thing that makes a timestamp
133	true — and the same holds for every PR number, sha and label a comment asserts:
134	resolve it, then post. (#143)
135	
136	**When a conformance check flags text, ask what a reader could act on before
137	reaching for an `accept`.** `claudinite-isolation` fired on `CLAUDE.md`'s
138	orientation header for spelling the vendored mount path. Nothing in that header
139	told a reader to go open the directory, so the path was pure decoration that
140	coupled a consumer file to a canon-internal layout — exactly the crossing the rule
141	exists to prevent, bought for nothing. Rewording to "vendored into this repo and
142	injected at session start" kept both facts a reader needs and lost only the
143	coupling. An `accept` entry is for a crossing that *must* exist; every one in this
144	repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` names a real constraint (a framework-fixed method
145	name, a deliberate broad-except, an optional-dependency availability probe). So
146	before adding one, delete the part the check is pointing at and see whether
147	anything actionable went with it — often nothing does. (#34)

# Working discipline

The working discipline that isn't itself a GitHub operation — general habits for how to approach a change, independent of any one project.

Start every requested change from the *problem*, not the solution — in any repository, not just this one. Before implementing, reach an explicit shared understanding with the owner of the problem the change is meant to solve **and** agreement that the requested change is the best way to solve it; a different fix, or no change at all, may serve the underlying problem better.

Open your reply to an owner comment with an explicit classification line — `Comment class: correction | feature | process-change | other` (`other` covers questions, approvals, and command phrases; a mixed comment names each part). The class decides where the change lands and what must exist before any fix. Put the class **alone on that line**: the line is scanned for *every* class token on it, so restating the menu to rule options out ("not a correction, feature request, or process-change") declares all of them, arming the gates those classes carry. Any explanation goes on the next line. This cannot be taken back — the transcript is append-only, and a clean re-declaration further down does not override the first.

1. **A correction** — you misunderstood something. Repair the shared understanding, then rework what the misread already touched; the artifact changes as much as the correction demands, but a correction never adds a new requirement or rule.

1	---
2	name: prose-to-checks
3	description: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
4	---
5	
6	# Convert existing prose to checks
7	
8	A completeness-critic over a repo's own packs: prose that is always-testable but was never converted
9	becomes a check, so the packs keep shedding context over time instead of only at the moment a rule is
10	first learned.
11	
12	## Two callers, differing only in scope
13	
14	- **The upgrade pass**, as the last step of a
15	  [growth-extract](../../tasks/growth-extract/task.md) run: the scope is the prose **that run just
16	  wrote**. Extraction already descends the promotion ladder per lesson, but a lesson written as prose
17	  under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides, so it gets asked once more before the
18	  PR opens. Never widen from here into the standing backlog.
19	- **The weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../../tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)**: the scope is the
20	  **standing backlog** — everything under the pack paths configured for this repo, which the task
21	  passes in its Context. A consuming repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) by
22	  default — projects don't improve core canon packs — while **Claudinite itself** also sweeps its core
23	  `packs/`. Read the prose under those paths (each pack's `RULES.md`, and any `SKILL.md` beside them).
24	
25	Plus on demand, when someone asks. Either way: never edit a read-only mounted canon pack under
26	`.claudinite/shared/`. Everything below is identical for both callers.
27	
28	## First gate — a working rule, not a product statement
29	
30	Before asking whether a rule is *testable*, ask whether it belongs to a pack at all: **does it govern
31	how we work, or state what the product does?** A pack — canon or local — homes the conventions,
32	gotchas and review discipline that recur across tasks whatever the feature happens to be. A rule
33	asserting which entities exist, what a surface must render, or that a feature's parts are wired to
34	each other is a **requirement**; its home is the project's executable spec and the suite that proves
35	it (the full rule lives in
36	[generate-project-instructions](../generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md)).
37	
38	This gate comes **first** because product statements sail through the check-the-world test below —
39	"this module must export `X`" has an obvious static signature. Converting one splits a feature's
40	definition across two systems and lands half of it in the one no test of the product ever reads.
41	Load-bearingness is not the test: a real gap in product coverage is a *requirements* gap.
42	
43	A product statement already sitting in pack prose is mis-homed, and a sweep is not the place to
44	re-home it. **Leave the prose and log it** as a mis-homed rule, the same way an un-checkable
45	candidate is logged — never cement it as a check.
46	
47	## What to look for — the check-the-world test
48	
49	For each rule that cleared the gate, ask the one question from
50	[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
51	signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**
52	
53	- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
54	  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
55	- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
56	  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
57	  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.
58	
59	**A static signature is necessary, not sufficient.** Both shapes the working-discipline rules bar
60	— a rule that pins today's code in place, and one derivable from the product's requirements —
61	answer *yes* here, so screen every candidate against that bar before converting it. Leave either
62	where it is; routing a requirement to the spec and its suite is its own change, not this sweep's.
63	
64	The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
65	part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.
66	
67	## How to convert one
68	
69	Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
70	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:
71	
72	> **The upgrade-pass caller lands inside growth-extract's own PR**, which auto-merges after CI — so the
73	> see-it-fail fixture is the only gate a converted check gets there. Convert only what you can prove;
74	> anything shakier stays prose and waits for the weekly sweep's reviewed PR.
75	
76	1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
77	   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
78	2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
79	   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
80	   doesn't ship.
81	3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
82	   directional by kind.
83	4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
84	   how you decide which paragraphs those are.
85	
86	**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
87	its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
88	which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
89	*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
90	check to the same fixture bar.
91	
92	When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
93	candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.
94	
95	## Coming out: the deletion test
96	
97	Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
98	deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
99	paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
100	how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
101	the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
102	either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.
103	
104	Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
105	activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
106	carries.
107	
108	The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
109	something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
110	encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
111	(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
112	that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant
113	went entirely — the check caught it and the testing-guide skill already listed the suites —
114	while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
115	`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.
116	
117	Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a
118	**reader**, not mechanized.
119	
120	## Bounds
121	
122	- **One PR, bounded surface** — the new rule module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixture, and the
123	  trimmed prose. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there.
124	- **Never delete a rule you didn't convert** — the deletion test is only ever asked of a rule a
125	  *landed* check now enforces.
126	- Run the suite and the sweep green before the PR goes up, and never push to `main` directly. The
127	  sweep opens its own PR for the owner's approval; the upgrade pass adds its conversion to the
128	  growth-extract PR already being opened, and opens none of its own.

`prose-to-checks` over this run's own additions only. 1	# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request
2	
3	How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
4	delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
5	run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
6	the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
7	your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
8	lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.
9	
10	## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest
11	
12	Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:
13	
14	- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
15	  applies to you.
16	- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
17	  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
18	  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
19	
20	## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference
21	
22	`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:
23	
24	- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
25	- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
26	  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
27	  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
28	- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
29	  materializing it is baselining's converge job, not yours.
30	- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
31	  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
32	  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the dispatch issue.
33	
34	## 2. Arm auto-merge
35	
36	Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
37	it once this repo's required checks pass.
38	
39	## 3. When the arm is rejected
40	
41	- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
42	  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
43	  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
44	  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
45	  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
46	- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
47	  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
48	  PR's **head sha**:
49	  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
50	    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
51	  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything

# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request

How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.

## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest

Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:

- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
  applies to you.
- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.

## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference

`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:

- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
  materializing it is baselining's converge job, not yours.
- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the dispatch issue.

## 2. Arm auto-merge

Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
it once this repo's required checks pass.

## 3. When the arm is rejected

- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
  PR's **head sha**:
  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the `merged-pr` ceiling — the trail
    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
    unseen check does not survive anything.

## Never

Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
are always legal outcomes.
